source_span: Net… more pressure on the Fed heading into Friday's CPI, which now feels pretty binary. September hike odds are back around 60%. A benign print gives them room to wait; a hot core print probably solidifies hike.
source_chain: August payrolls come in firmer than expected with unemployment steady at 4.1%, therefore pressure builds on the Fed and September hike odds rise to ~60%, therefore Friday's CPI becomes the binary decider — invalidation: a benign print lets the Fed wait, a hot core print solidifies a hike.
pulse_chain: August payrolls beat sharply (162k vs 55k) with unemployment held at 4.1%, therefore September hike odds jump from ~50% to ~60% (futures 63%), therefore Friday's CPI is the deciding factor, which Goldman's European desk reads as binary — invalidation: a mild print lets the Fed wait, a hot core reading likely seals the hike — with the specific decisive threshold (core PCE ~0.30%/2.8% per JPM's read of Waller, ~25bp per Goldman's Treasury desk) laid over the top and bank forecasts (UBS two hikes, BofA 75bp, DB underpricing, GS/MS hold) arrayed around it.
why: The theme's setup, direction, and invalidation (binary CPI outcome deciding hike-vs-hold) reproduce Goldman's note almost verbatim, and every extension layered on top (JPM's Waller/PCE bar, Goldman Treasury's 25bp line, UBS's forecast flip, DB's ISM prices-paid argument) checks out against its own correctly-named source document even where a couple of inline citation-ID tags point to an adjacent doc rather than the true source.
